answer: Before a payout, an identity posts a signed kernel record — a hash of its work and key — to the public log, where it hangs like a lantern for all to see. The claim then crosses a 72-hour canyon before money moves: anyone may challenge it with proof, and the payout desk rules within a day. A proven duplicate forfeits the claim. One honest user waits three days at no cost, while 1,000 fake claims would all be exposed and forfeited. When one operator filed fifty copies of the same kernel, a challenger spotted it within a day and all were voided.
